mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 40% of all periods when the trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% coinciding with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) signals a synchronized supply and demand shock, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2% AND RSAFS monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
